workflows.name: Walkability snapshot for a listing: nearest amenity on OpenStreetMap plus the area on Wikipedia
steps: In the OpenStreetMap tab, click the search box, type "{amenity} near {address}" and press Enter; pick the first result and note its name
Click the directions icon, choose walking (Foot), set From to {address} and To to that {amenity}, and read the walking distance and time
Switch to the Wikipedia tab, search "{neighborhood}" and open the article; read its first sentence
Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "{address}: nearest {amenity} <name>, <distance>, <minutes> walk. {neighborhood}: <short description>" and press Enter

workflows.name: Source a candidate from GitHub and their blog, then email the hiring manager
steps: In the GitHub tab, click the search box, type {username}, and open the user profile {username}
Note the follower count and the most-starred pinned repository; open it and note its stars and main language
Open a new tab, go to {blog} and note the title of the most recent post, then close the tab
Switch to the Mail tab, click To and type hiring@example.com, click Subject and type "Lead for {role}: {username}"
Click Body and type "{username}: <followers> followers, top repo <repo> (<stars> stars, <language>), latest post: <title>." Do not click Send. Click Discard

workflows.name: Fact-check a person on Wikipedia and an old page on the Wayback Machine
steps: In the Wikipedia tab, search "{person}" and open the article; note the birth date and current or last position
Switch to the Wayback Machine tab, type {site} in the search box and press Enter
Pick the year {year} in the timeline, click a highlighted day in the calendar and open the snapshot
Note the page title and one headline on the snapshot, then click Back to return to the Wayback Machine home
Switch to Notes, click "New note", type "{person}: born <date>, <position>. {site} in {year}: <headline>" and press Enter

noise.description: Open a new tab, go to bbc.com/news, scroll through the headlines, open one story, skim it, close the tab
Open a new tab, go to weather.com, search the forecast for New York, look at it, close the tab
Abandoned attempt: in the OpenStreetMap tab, type "coffee near Union Square" in the search box, look at the results, then give up and clear the search box
Wander: click through the Notes, Mail and GitHub tabs without doing anything, scroll the Notes list
Open a new tab, go to news.ycombinator.com, scroll the front page, open one comment thread, close the tab
